Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section II in 1 1/2 hours; you are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section II, answer all questions choosing EITHER parts a, b and c OR parts d, e and f of each question. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration of free fall, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Calculators are allowed.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Distinguish between:

(i) an intrinsic and an extrinsic semiconductor. *[2 marks]*

(ii) a p-type and an n-type semiconductor. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) An **intrinsic** semiconductor is a **pure** semiconductor (for example pure silicon or germanium) with no impurity added; its conductivity is small and comes from equal numbers of electrons and holes produced by heat. An **extrinsic** semiconductor is a pure semiconductor to which a **small amount of impurity has been added (doping)** to increase its conductivity.

(ii) A **p-type** semiconductor is doped with a **trivalent** element (three outer electrons, e.g. boron), which creates **holes**; the **majority charge carriers are holes** (positive). An **n-type** semiconductor is doped with a **pentavalent** element (five outer electrons, e.g. phosphorus), which gives free electrons; the **majority charge carriers are electrons** (negative).

questions.enonce_markdown: Name an element that can be added to a crystal of pure silicon to produce an n-type semiconductor. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: **Phosphorus** (or arsenic or antimony): a Group V element with five outer electrons.
